Hello,

Thank you, I received the Overclocking hardware for the Hammer Miner Thor X1, but I have no idea how to install/ upgrade my Hammer Miner Thor X1.

Please can you send me more details as to how to do it.

Hi Warrick,

Happy to walk you through it, and there is one important thing to flag first.

The O. Bundle contains a Mean Well LRS-350-12 power supply (12V, 29A), a thermal paste syringe, nine aluminium heatsinks and two alcohol pads. The heatsinks and the paste are the parts that apply to your Thor X1. The M. Well unit is an open frame 12V supply meant for miners that take a 12V DC input, and the Thor X1 is powered over USB-C instead, so that supply is not the right power source for this machine. Please do not try to adapt or rewire it to the USB-C port. For the X1 itself, use a good quality USB-C PD adapter with plenty of headroom over the roughly 46W the unit draws, so around 65W or more, with a cable rated for that current. A supply that sags under load is the single most common cause of a miner dropping out or restarting once you push it.

For the heatsinks, the sequence is simple. Shut the miner down from the dashboard, unplug it at the wall and give it fifteen minutes to cool. Open the shell and look at the small components near the chip: the voltage regulator stages, the power stage and the controller are the ones that benefit. Wipe each one you plan to cover with an alcohol pad and let it dry fully. Put a very thin smear of paste on the heatsink base, enough to fill the gap and no more, then press the heatsink straight down and hold it for twenty or thirty seconds. Keep each heatsink sitting on one component only, never bridging two, and make sure none of them touch the fan, the fan wires or the shell when you close it up. Then reassemble, plug it back in on the USB-C supply and let it run at stock settings for an hour while you watch the temperatures in the dashboard. You want a stable baseline before you change any clocks.

On the firmware and the actual overclock, the Thor X1 firmware lives on the HammerMiner X1 repository on GitHub.
The 1.0.6 release from September 2026 changed the overclocking mode into a performance mode
, so check which version your unit reports in its web dashboard and update to the current one before you tune anything, as the controls differ between versions. Once you are on current firmware, raise the frequency in small steps from the dashboard, leave it for twenty minutes at each step and watch chip temperature and rejected shares. The moment the hashrate stops climbing, the temperature climbs sharply or rejects appear, go back one step and stay there. Raise voltage only if the unit becomes unstable at a frequency it otherwise reaches, and only in the smallest increments the interface allows.

One thing I owe you straight:
the Thor X1 is rated at 3.2 TH/s, and running it above that, including any turbo or boost mode, is overclocking, which runs hotter, needs good airflow and voids the warranty
. The heatsinks and fresh paste are a sensible thing to fit either way, since they help the unit run cooler at stock too.

I have passed the power supply question to JD, our hardware lead, so he can confirm the best power option for an overclocked X1, and a colleague is picking that up today. If you want a faster answer in the meantime, our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf is very active and you can mention @nullhashrate, who is JD.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
